long_biography.plain_text:
Haremlique Istanbul began with Caroline Koç and Banu Yentür designing bed and bath linens inspired by Istanbul and Ottoman imagery. Koç had grown up in Izmir's Giraud family, whose businesses manufactured textiles, and saw a gap between Turkey's production expertise and its international luxury-brand presence. The partners launched the company in 2008 and shared practical work as well as creative decisions: at trade fairs, Yentür folded linens while Koç ironed them.

Koç also developed an art collection that brings Chinese antiques and midcentury furniture together with contemporary works. Her choices grew bolder over time, placing art by Marc Quinn and Taner Ceylan within an older decorative setting. Among the works she selected are photographs from Mat Collishaw's Last Meal on Death Row series.
long_biography.html:
Haremlique Istanbul began with Caroline Koç and Banu Yentür designing bed and bath linens inspired by Istanbul and Ottoman imagery. Koç had grown up in Izmir's Giraud family, whose businesses manufactured textiles, and saw a gap between Turkey's production expertise and its international luxury-brand presence. The partners launched the company in 2008 and shared practical work as well as creative decisions: at trade fairs, Yentür folded linens while Koç ironed them.

Koç also developed an art collection that brings Chinese antiques and midcentury furniture together with contemporary works. Her choices grew bolder over time, placing art by Marc Quinn and Taner Ceylan within an older decorative setting. Among the works she selected are photographs from Mat Collishaw's Last Meal on Death Row series.
